The pinned engine reference has no core, file-I/O or threading module, so every engine claim here rests either on a probe run on the installed 4.7.2 editor on 2026-10-28 (marked **probed**) or on training knowledge (marked **UNVERIFIED**, with the spike that settles it). No game code exists. All probes were synthetic, headless, on a development machine with an editor binary; none is a release-export measurement. Revised 2026-10-28 after the engine review (E1 to E12), the technical-director review (T1 to T12) and cross-ADR rulings TD-04, TD-05, TD-07, TD-09, TD-10, TD-11, TD-12, TD-15, TD-24, TD-25, TD-26, TD-27, TD-33, TD-34 (see Review Log); a second probe round the same day settled `make_read_only` depth, `duplicate_deep`, packed-array aliasing, `encode_s64` on an empty array and uppercase `hex_decode`.
@@END
@@REPLACE Claude (author), running under
Claude (author), running under `modes.automation: autonomous` (`project.yaml`); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR. Engine-specialist review (BLOCKING item E1, twelve items in all) and technical-director review (verdict CONCERNS, five BLOCKING items T1 to T6) were returned on 2026-10-28 and applied in this revision; a confirming re-review is still owed before Accept. See Review Log.
@@END
@@REPLACE Sixty-five requirements from seventeen GDDs
Over a hundred requirements from seventeen GDDs (the 65 rows of `tr-baseline.md` plus the TR-saveload-028 to 042 gap rows and the cross-system rows the traceability matrix assigns here) need a save file that is self-verifying, written without ever endangering a good generation, versioned from the first build, and paired with a per-slot `restore_epoch` that re-keys threat draws on death without letting quit or death be a reroll oracle. This ADR fixes one container (8-byte magic, JSON header, `var_to_bytes` block payloads, SHA-256 trailer), a ring of three generations written by one `Thread` per job that the main thread only polls, a two-level version scheme (container migrated by Save/Load, blocks by their owners), a reserved PROFILE side file in the same container (built at the first PROFILE block, not at MVP), and a `restore_epoch` held in two alternating checksummed files that is made durable before every `request_restore`. The service is a tree-free `RefCounted` in `src/save/`; a thin `SaveHost` node in `src/game/` polls it once per frame and owns the window-close interception. Settings persistence is out of scope.
@@END
@@REPLACE | **Knowledge Risk** |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. The APIs used (`FileAccess`, `DirAccess`, `Thread`, `Mutex`, `HashingContext`, `var_to_bytes`, `bytes_to_var`, `JSON`, `PackedByteArray.encode_*`/`decode_*`, `hex_encode`/`hex_decode`) all predate 4.4, and `breaking-changes.md` lists only one relevant change (4.4: every `FileAccess.store_*` returns `bool`, sourced). But the reference has no module for them, so behaviour on Windows (rename, sharing, thread exit) is training knowledge unless probed here. The 4.7 typed-return override rule applies to overrides of engine methods with typed returns (`_to_string`, `_get_configuration_warnings`, `_get`, `_get_property_list`, ...) in Save/Load classes, which must return on every path; the outcome handler (ADR-0002 line 206) returns `CompletionToken` on every path. |
@@END
@@SUBST may appear inside snapshots; it survives the encoder (probed). ==> may appear inside snapshots; its values round-trip through the encoder (probed; type preservation is not asserted, the walk checks decoded elements).
@@END
@@REPLACE | **Probes run 2026-10-28
| **Probes run 2026-10-28 (4.7.2.stable.mono, Windows 11, headless, scratch directory outside the repo). `[n%]` = the engine review's estimate that the claim is correct and reproducible on 4.7.2** | (1) `DirAccess.rename` and `rename_absolute` over an existing, unlocked target: `OK`, target content replaced, source gone [85%]. **The replacement is probably remove-then-rename on Windows, not an atomic `MoveFileEx`** (recollection of `DirAccessWindows::rename`, about 65%, **UNVERIFIED** against the 4.7.2 source); probes (1) and (2) cannot tell the two apart, so rename-over is never described as atomic or as "old file intact" across a crash (§ 1.5). (2) Rename over a target held open by another `FileAccess` handle (READ or READ_WRITE): `ERR_FAILED` (1), target intact; rename of a source held open: `ERR_FAILED`; `remove_absolute` of a READ-held or WRITE-held file: `ERR_FAILED` [85%]. (3) `FileAccess.open(path, WRITE)` is **not exclusive**: a second WRITE open of the same path succeeded (WRITE mode truncates per the documented flag semantics; the truncation itself was not probed); READ-open while WRITE-open succeeded; WRITE-open while READ-held succeeded [90%]. (4) `store_buffer`, `store_32` return `true`; `store_buffer` on a READ handle returns `false` with `get_error()` = 13 (`ERR_FILE_CANT_WRITE`); `get_buffer` past the end returns the available bytes and sets `eof_reached` and error 18 [90%]. (5) `var_to_bytes` of an `int` above 2^53 (2^53+1) and of `PackedInt64Array` round-trips exactly [95%]; **`var_to_bytes({"o": RefCounted.new()})` silently succeeds, encoding an `EncodedObjectAsID`, and `bytes_to_var` returns it as an `Object`** [90%]; `Vector2i`, `StringName`, typed `Array[int]`, typed `Dictionary[String, int]`, `NaN` and `INF` round-trip as **values; type preservation is not asserted** [70%]. (6) `bytes_to_var` of `var_to_bytes_with_objects` output returns `null` and logs an engine `ERROR` (`ERR_UNAUTHORIZED`); garbage and empty input return `null` and log an engine `ERROR` [90%]. (7) Two dictionaries with the same entries in different insertion order encode to **different** bytes [95%]. (8) `JSON.new().parse` returns every number as `float`; `9007199254740993` parses to `9007199254740992.0` [95%]. (9) `"ffffffffffffffff".hex_to_int()` logs an error and returns `INT64_MAX`; `String.hex_decode()` plus `PackedByteArray.decode_u64` / `decode_s64` is exact (a 64-bit pattern with the top bit set reads as a negative GDScript `int`) [85%]. (10) `PackedByteArray` has **no** `crc32`; a 4-byte bitwise CRC32 in GDScript matched the standard check vector (`0xCBF43926` for `"123456789"`); the cost is **of order microseconds** per call (the first-run figure of about 1 microsecond is implausibly low, [40%], and irrelevant to the design) [90% for the check vector]. (11) `Thread.start(callable.bind(packed_bytes, path))` works, the payload size is unchanged on the caller (this shows the worker did not mutate it, **not** copy semantics, see probe 16), `is_alive()` polls, `wait_to_finish()` on a finished thread returns the callable's return value immediately; a process that calls `quit()` with a thread still **sleeping** 8 s exited in 0.68 s with a `~Thread` WARNING and an ObjectDB leak report [80%; sleeping worker only, a worker blocked in a syscall or mid-`store_buffer` is untested]. (12) `OS.is_process_running(OS.get_process_id())` is `true` [95%]. (13) Synthetic timings, dev machine, not a release export: `HashingContext` SHA-256 over 100 KiB 1.35 ms, 300 KiB 0.72 ms, 2 MiB 4.9 ms; `var_to_bytes` of 32 synthetic blocks (860 416 B) 1.93 ms; `Dictionary.duplicate(true)` of the same 2.0 ms; `bytes_to_var` of the same 3.5 ms [70%]. |
| **Probes run 2026-10-28, second round (post-review, same machine and build)** | (14) `Dictionary.make_read_only()` is **shallow**: the parent reports read-only, a nested `Dictionary` and a nested `Array` do not, and a write through the nested `Dictionary` succeeds (settles OQ-C: assume shallow). (15) `Array.duplicate_deep()` and `Dictionary.duplicate_deep()` **exist on 4.7.2** and copy nested containers (the engine reference mentions `duplicate_deep` for Resources only); `duplicate(true)` is also available and is what this ADR names. (16) A `PackedByteArray` assigned to a second variable **shares storage**: an `append` through one name is visible through the other, so packed arrays are reference-shared in GDScript, not copy-on-write. (17) `PackedByteArray.encode_s64(0, v)` on an **empty** array logs an engine `ERROR` (`p_offset > size - 8`) and writes nothing; the array must be `resize(8)`'d first; `encode_s64` returns `void`. (18) `String.hex_decode()` accepts uppercase hex. **Not probed (UNVERIFIED):** `Thread.start` error codes, `get_string_from_utf8` on invalid UTF-8, a `Thread` freed while alive, a worker blocked in a syscall at exit, kill between remove and rename. |
| **Concurrency semantics** | Packed arrays, Arrays and Dictionaries are reference-shared across threads in GDScript (probe 16; the `PackedByteArray` documentation says packed arrays are "always passed by reference"; ADR-0005 states "packed arrays alias by reference"); **immutability is enforced by ownership transfer, not by the engine** (§ 1.6). |
@@END
@@REPLACE | **Verification Required** |
| **Verification Required** | The spike is split so the gate can be satisfied before any owner block exists (TD-ADR T3). **SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT (gates Accept; architecture § Spikes that gate ADRs):** on a **Windows `template_release` export** with Defender real-time scanning on, a OneDrive-redirected `user://` and a slow HDD: (a) `DirAccess.rename` over a target held by an antivirus or indexer handle (the READ-held probe is only a proxy): return code, retry success rate, target intact; (b) whether a crash between the two renames of the generation swap ever leaves neither file, **and** what a kill between the remove and the rename of a rename-over leaves for `campaign.json` (kill the process at every step of T-4 and inside the rename-over; the deterministic fault-injection harness of AC-SL-30); (c) `FileAccess.flush()` followed by close and re-read: whether bytes reach the media is **UNVERIFIED** and cannot be proven by software, so the ring is the answer, not the verify; (d) quit during a write: wall time from `request_shutdown` to process exit with a worker blocked inside a slow `store_buffer` and inside a `rename` (the probe used a sleeping worker), on a dev build and on a release export, including whether the worker touches freed singletons (`ProjectSettings`, `OS`) while the engine tears down; (e) the `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` frame poll at `HOST_SERVICE` priority while the kernel is `PAUSED`, `SAVING` and `LOADING` (needs a scene tree; **UNVERIFIED**), and the `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST` path with `auto_accept_quit` false; (f) the **synthetic hitch**: a 14-block fixture sized to SL-19 (86 to 300 KiB) through the real `var_to_bytes`, hand-off and a stand-in `H64`, plus the **type-walk timing** (target: walk at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes; the walk runs on the hot-copy worker when it can); (g) the `campaign.lock` mechanism of § 1.7 on **any Linux build**, where rename of an open file is expected to succeed (**UNVERIFIED**); (h) whether a `Mutex`-guarded status record plus `is_alive()` polling is race-free under a forced stall (a thread sleeping inside the critical section); (i) a loop that kills the process mid-rename-over and counts "target missing" outcomes (informs the accepted exposure of § 1.5). **SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (does not gate Accept; gates the Vertical Slice milestone):** item (f) re-run on the **real** owner blocks on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK with the kernel's real capture-time hash, which decides whether rung 1 or 2 of § 1.9 is needed. **SAVE-WRK-2 (does not gate acceptance):** RAM held by the two hot decoded copies (SL-11) at the VS-A size. |
@@END
EOF

@@REPLACE Sixty-five requirements from seventeen GDDs
Over a hundred requirements from seventeen GDDs (the 65 rows of `tr-baseline.md`, the TR-saveload-028 to 042 gap rows and the cross-system rows the traceability matrix assigns here) need a save file that is self-verifying, written without ever endangering a good generation, versioned from the first build, and paired with a per-slot `restore_epoch` that re-keys threat draws on death without letting quit or death be a reroll oracle. This ADR fixes one container (8-byte magic, JSON header, `var_to_bytes` block payloads, SHA-256 trailer), a ring of three generations written by one `Thread` per job that the main thread only polls, a two-level version scheme (container migrated by Save/Load, blocks by their owners), a reserved PROFILE side file in the same container (built at the first PROFILE block, not at MVP), and a `restore_epoch` held in two alternating checksummed files that is made durable before every `request_restore`. The service is a tree-free `RefCounted` in `src/save/`; a thin `SaveHost` node in `src/game/` polls it once per frame and owns the window-close interception. Settings persistence is out of scope.
@@END

| **Probes run 2026-10-28, second round (post-review, same machine and build)** | (14) `Dictionary.make_read_only()` is **shallow**: the parent reports read-only, a nested `Dictionary` and a nested `Array` do not, and a write through the nested `Dictionary` succeeds (settles OQ-C: assume shallow). (b) whether a crash between the two renames of the generation swap ever leaves neither file, **and** what a kill between the remove and the rename of a rename-over leaves for `campaign.json` (kill the process at every step of T-4 and inside the rename-over; the deterministic fault-injection harness of AC-SL-30); (c) `FileAccess.flush()` followed by close and re-read: whether bytes reach the media is **UNVERIFIED** and cannot be proven by software, so the ring is the answer, not the verify; (d) quit during a write: wall time from `request_shutdown` to process exit with a worker blocked inside a slow `store_buffer` and inside a `rename` (the probe used a sleeping worker), on a dev build and on a release export, including whether the worker touches freed singletons (`ProjectSettings`, `OS`) while the engine tears down; (e) the `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` frame poll at `HOST_SERVICE` priority while the kernel is `PAUSED`, `SAVING` and `LOADING` (needs a scene tree; **UNVERIFIED**), and the `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST` path with `auto_accept_quit` false; (f) the **synthetic hitch**: a 14-block fixture sized to SL-19 (86 to 300 KiB) through the real `var_to_bytes`, hand-off and a stand-in `H64`, plus the **type-walk timing** (target: walk at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes; the walk runs on the hot-copy worker when it can); (g) the `campaign.lock` mechanism of § 1.7 on **any Linux build**, where rename of an open file is expected to succeed (**UNVERIFIED**); (h) whether a `Mutex`-guarded status record plus `is_alive()` polling is race-free under a forced stall (a thread sleeping inside the critical section); (i) a loop that kills the process mid-rename-over and counts "target missing" outcomes (informs the accepted exposure of § 1.5). **SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (does not gate Accept; gates the Vertical Slice milestone):** item (f) re-run on the **real** owner blocks on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK with the kernel's real capture-time hash, which decides whether rung 1 or 2 of § 1.9 is needed. **SAVE-WRK-2 (does not gate acceptance):** RAM held by the two hot decoded copies (SL-11) at the VS-A size. |
@@END
@@REPLACE | **Depends On** |
| **Depends On** | ADR-0001 (frame order, `ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE`, boundary service, quit transition, no autoload; Proposed), ADR-0002 § 6 (`ControlHandle`: `request_snapshot() -> void` with the result delivered to the registered outcome handler; the snapshot `ControlOutcome` extended with `T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, `hash_algo` and per-block `block_ids`, `schema_versions`, `block_state_hashes`, `enc_lens` (TD-05); `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)`, `request_new_game`, `request_shutdown`; Proposed), ADR-0003 (block descriptors, `SnapshotContext`, the kernel state machine incl. `SAVING` and `LOADING`, fault domain 1 = `save_load`, a BOOTING-only registrar facet limited to `register_fault_domain` for a host service, kernel codes `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` and `CAPTURE_ERROR`; Proposed), **ADR-0005** (`H64` and `hash_algo` 2, `Hex64` in `src/shared/det/`, the uncached capture-time hashes, the canonical TLV used as hash input; **must be Accepted before ADR-0006 is Accepted**), ADR-0007 (the pipeline that loads Save/Load's tuning table and block-version data file; `catalogue_version`; Proposed), **ADR-0010** (IO-02 `Thread` allowance in `src/save/` only, SIM-02 allow-list including `system_wall_clock.gd`, SIM-12, § 8.6 log allow-list, `SaveHost` placement in `src/game/`; **must be Accepted before ADR-0006 is Accepted**). |
@@END
@@REPLACE | **Enables** |
| **Enables** | ADR-0016 (restore ordering and cross-block verification consumes the staged payload and the two-phase rule), every system ADR that registers a persisted block (ADR-0011, 0013, 0015, 0017, 0019, 0022, 0023, 0025, 0026, 0027: they implement the § 1.2 contract and the § 2.2 schema chain), ADR-0021 (the weld transaction's pending-window behaviour at save), ADR-0030 (Chart Table menu flows over the host API; `SettingsStore` and its port, § Scope), ADR-0031 (dev-only `dump-save`, `save_now`, `load(generation)` gating). ADR-0002 and ADR-0007 list ADR-0006 under their Enables (ADR-0002 does; ADR-0007 is asked to, TD-27). **Related, not a dependency:** ADR-0004 (the trigger and touch-serial source; Save/Load subscribes to nothing, § 1.12). |
@@END
@@REPLACE | **Blocks** |
| **Blocks** | Epics: Save/Load & Versioned Format; Chart Table boot flows (New Game, Continue, Save & Quit); Player Controller death hand-off (`TR-pc-022`); every story that registers a `persist` block (needs the § 1.2 payload rules and § 2.2 version rules). |
@@END
@@REPLACE | **Ordering Note** |
| **Ordering Note** | **Acceptance order:** ADR-0001, 0002, 0003, 0005, 0007 and 0010 Accepted, then SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT passed (the SLICE half does not gate, § Verification Required). ADR-0005 owns the canonical byte encoding, `H64` (`hash_algo` 2), `Hex64` and `rng_derive_epoch`; this ADR fixes only where the hash is stored and that `restore_epoch` is never an input to it. ADR-0005 § 5.4 makes the snapshot capture an always-uncached path; Save/Load never decides on a cached hash. ADR-0004 owns the notification classes; Save/Load is a polling control-plane caller with no subscription (§ 1.12). ADR-0010 owns the source layout and the lint; it carries the `Thread` allowance (IO-02, `src/save/` only), the deferred-call ban (SIM-12), the wall-clock allow-list (SIM-02) and the `SaveHost` row of § 1.1. **Scope edge with ADR-0003:** the kernel owns the states `SAVING`/`LOADING` and capture cost against `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`; this ADR owns what happens to the captured payload and the staged restore payload. **Scope edge with ADR-0007:** Save/Load's knob range checks and structural invariants (TR-saveload-024) are ADR-0007 § 2.5; the cross-check of block versions against the live registry (§ 2.3) needs the registry and so is Save/Load's own boot check. **Scope note (TD-26):** settings persistence (`DisplaySettings` and similar) is out of scope. It is never kernel state and never in the save container. ADR-0030 decides `SettingsStore`; because of IO-01, its file I/O goes through an injected port whose implementation lives in `src/save/`. |
@@END
@@SUBST - **Exactly one thread boundary** exists ==> - **Exactly one thread boundary** exists
@@END
@@REPLACE - **Exactly one thread boundary**
- **Exactly one thread boundary** exists (architecture § Data Flow 7): the save writer. `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool`, `Mutex` and `Semaphore` are allowed only in `src/save/` (ADR-0010 IO-02), and `call_deferred`, `set_deferred`, `call_thread_safe` and `Engine.get_main_loop` are banned in `src/save/` as everywhere else in the foundation layers (SIM-12); this ADR cites those rules and does not restate them. The only cross-thread payload is a `PackedByteArray` (or `PackedInt64Array`) **handed over by value and never mutated by either side afterwards**, plus pre-globalised absolute path strings, ints and a header template built for the job (TR-saveload-007; § 1.6 states the ownership rule, because the engine does not enforce one).
@@END
@@SUBST - **Integer-only simulation** (ADR-0005 forward); ==> - **Integer-only simulation** (ADR-0005);
@@END
@@REPLACE - **No wall clock in any sim decision**
- **No wall clock in any sim decision** (kernel H9; ADR-0010 SIM-02): every millisecond I/O timeout in this ADR (`WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS`, `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS`, `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS`, `RENAME_RETRY_DELAY_MS`) reads the injected `Clock` port (`src/kernel/ports/clock.gd`, `now_us()`; `FakeClock` in tests) and changes no sim state (SL-23). The one wall-time value, `created_unix` and the time `SaveInfo` displays, comes from the `WallClock` port (`src/save/wall_clock.gd`, `now_unix() -> int`; sole implementation `src/game/system_wall_clock.gd`, ADR-0010 TD-11), injected into `SaveService.setup()` only. It is display metadata and is **never** an ordering key (the generation number is the only order), a gate, a hash input or a sim input.
@@END
@@SUBST A quit that waits for its write by polling, with a timeout, and never hangs the process on a stuck worker. ==> A quit that waits for its write by polling, with a timeout, and never hangs the process on a stuck worker; the window close button, Alt+F4 and OS shutdown take the same path (§ 1.6).
@@END

@@REPLACE - **Model.** One `Thread` per `WriteJob`
- **Model.** One `Thread` per `WriteJob`, its handle held on a `RefCounted` `WriteJob` that also carries the status record, started with `thread.start(WriteWorker.run.bind(block_bytes, header_template, paths, ints))` (the typed bound form of a static function, not the stringly `Callable(WriteWorker, "run")`). **`Thread.start` returns an `Error`; anything other than `OK` (for example `ERR_CANT_CREATE` when the OS refuses a thread) ends the job at once as `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED`**, with no worker and no `.tmp`. **`WorkerThreadPool` is rejected**: it offers no timed wait and its tasks cannot be abandoned individually (training knowledge; **UNVERIFIED** against 4.7, ADR-0010 may confirm). The Save/Load module is the **one** place `Thread` is legal (ADR-0010 IO-02, `src/save/` only).
- **Ownership transfer, not copy-on-write (engine review E1).** Packed arrays, Arrays and Dictionaries are reference-shared across threads in GDScript (probe 16); the engine enforces no immutability, so this ADR does. (1) At hand-off the main thread **holds no alias** to any handed-over object: a hot copy, a `SaveInfo`, a retry buffer or the `ControlOutcome` payload each count as an alias. A buffer the main thread must keep is handed over as `.duplicate()` (packed array) or `.duplicate(true)` (Array, Dictionary) instead. (2) The main thread never appends to, resizes or reuses a handed-over object afterwards. (3) The worker **never mutates, appends to or resizes an argument**; it builds new arrays for everything it produces. (4) The handed-over `Array[PackedByteArray]` and header template may be marked `make_read_only()` as a convenience; it is shallow (probe 14) and covers the top-level container only, so rules (1) and (2) carry the weight. A unit test hands a buffer off, mutates a retained alias and asserts the worker output is unchanged; it fails if an alias is kept without `.duplicate()`. The probe that "the caller's array is unchanged" shows only that the worker did not mutate it.
@@END
@@REPLACE - **Status record.**
- **Status record.** `{state, write_epoch, generation, position, result_code, finish_or_abort, quit_requested}` guarded by one `Mutex`; the worker writes `state` at each T-4 stage and reads `quit_requested` between stages (it starts no new stage once set and leaves the `.tmp` to T-6); the main thread reads the record and writes only `finish_or_abort` (SL-10, `DOWNED` entry) and `quit_requested`. The worker never calls `call_deferred` (SIM-12), never touches a `Node`, never calls back (probed: no callback needed). The worker receives **only pre-globalised absolute filesystem paths**: `ProjectSettings.globalize_path` runs on the main thread, and the worker never resolves `user://` itself, so it touches no engine singleton for path lookup.
@@END
@@REPLACE - **Polling.**
- **Polling.** `SaveHost._process` calls `SaveService.poll_frame()` once per frame. `SaveHost` is the thin `Node` of `src/game/save_host.gd` (L4, ADR-0010 § 1.1, beside `KernelHost`) with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and `process_priority = ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE` (-40: after `TICK_DRIVER` -50, before `PRESENTATION` 0; the one constant, named and valued in ADR-0001, TD-04); it is a known non-presentation node in the KRN-05 boot walk, holds no `FileAccess` and no `Thread`, and owns nothing but the injected `SaveService`. `SaveService`, `WriteJob`, `WriteWorker`, `PreCheck`, `SaveCodec`, `SlotEpoch`, `RegistryView` and `BuildConstants` are `RefCounted` under `src/save/` with no tree access, so ADR-0010 SIM-01 keeps its no-waiver status. **There is no separate tick-boundary poll:** the frame poll after the driver is the only observation point. A `request_snapshot` is served at the next boundary service, before any tick, so state read at the end of frame N is exactly the state captured in frame N+1 (OQ-F closed). That the frame poll fires in `PAUSED` and `LOADING` is **UNVERIFIED** (needs a scene tree; SAVE-WRK-1 e).
@@END
@@REPLACE - **Reaping.**
- **Reaping and lifetime.** Each poll calls `wait_to_finish()` **only** on a job whose thread reports `not is_alive()` (probed: returns at once with the callable's value). @@REPLACE **3.1 Ownership and storage.**
**3.1 Ownership and storage.** Save/Load owns `restore_epoch`, an unsigned 32-bit integer (an `int` in `[0, 2^32 - 1]`) starting at 0 at `new_game` (SL-18); it has exactly one owner and registry entry. It lives in a per-slot **pair of side files**, `user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch_a.bin` and `slot_epoch_b.bin`, each **12 bytes: the epoch as `u32` LE, a sequence number `seq` as `u32` LE, then the CRC32 of those 8 bytes as `u32` LE** (the GDD / TR-saveload-020 format of `u32` plus CRC32 gains the `seq` field; GDD sync). The reader takes the valid file (size 12, CRC matches) with the higher `seq`; the writer always overwrites the **older** file in place (an invalid file, or the lower `seq`) with `seq = max + 1`, flushes, closes, re-reads and checks the CRC (that re-read is the `EPOCH_DURABLE` report). **No rename and no remove is involved**, so there is never an instant with no valid epoch file: a kill mid-write corrupts only the file being written and the other still holds the previous durable value. (A single file replaced by rename-over would, on Windows, probably be remove-then-rename, § 1.5, open a window in which the file is absent, and let the rebuild rule of § 3.4 yield `max(header copy) + 1`, which can be lower than an epoch already advanced, for example after two deaths with no autosave between them, replaying one set of threat draws; engine review E2.) `seq` saturates at 2^32 - 1, unreachable in practice because the epoch saturates first. `SlotEpoch.encode` calls `resize(12)` before any `encode_u32` (probe 17). **CRC32 is hand-rolled** (polynomial `0xEDB88320`, init and final XOR `0xFFFFFFFF`, bitwise, over 8 bytes): `PackedByteArray` has no `crc32` (probed), the scripted loop matched the standard check vector, its cost is of order microseconds, and a truncated hash was rejected as a gratuitous change to the GDD format. The vector `crc32("123456789") == 0xCBF43926` is a unit test. The files are in no generation, so no generation's bytes, trailer, `state_hash` or any key derived from them changes after `VERIFYING`; this is what makes SL-12's REBASED baseline key stable (R14). Each WORLD generation's header carries a **read-only write-time copy** (`restore_epoch`, an int below 2^32) used only by the rebuild rule of § 3.4; it is never rewritten.
@@END
@@REPLACE **3.3 Durable before the restore is requested
**3.3 Durable before the restore is requested (R14, with the polling decided).** After selection, pre-check and staging, Save/Load computes the new value and hands the `slot_epoch` write (the older of the two files, § 3.1) to the worker **as its own job**, never queued behind a generation write or an abandoned job, and polls it once per frame from `poll_frame` (never blocking, never joined). Only on `EPOCH_DURABLE` does it call `ControlHandle.request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)`, so the kernel's `LOADING` holds no wait on Save/Load I/O and stays atomic within one boundary service. **3.6 Staging and hot copy.** Candidate selection (SL-8), the death-stub's one synchronous attempt per candidate and the newest and preceding **hot decoded copies** (SL-11) stand as written; the hot copies are held by Save/Load and are never handed to a worker (a retained alias of a handed-over buffer is forbidden, § 1.6). @@AFTER - **Status:** remains Proposed.

## Registry Candidates

Reviewable candidates for `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`, corrected by the 2026-10-28 rulings (TD-33); the orchestrator merges them serially once the revisions land. All entries are `status: active` while this ADR is Proposed and become binding on Acceptance. `restore_epoch` has **one** entry, here; ADR-0005 references it and does not duplicate it.

```yaml
state_ownership:
  - state: restore_epoch
    owner_system: save-load (SaveService)
    interface: "u32 in the per-slot pair user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch_a.bin and slot_epoch_b.bin (12 bytes each: u32 LE epoch, u32 LE seq, u32 LE hand-rolled CRC32 poly 0xEDB88320 of the first 8 bytes); the reader takes the valid file with the higher seq, the writer overwrites the older file in place (no rename, no remove); durable (EPOCH_DURABLE re-read) before request_restore; reaches the sim only as the request_restore / request_new_game argument and the read-only non-persisted non-hashed kernel.clock view (T, world_seed, restore_epoch), read only inside RngFacet.draw_epoch; each WORLD generation header carries a read-only write-time recovery copy; advance = min(2^32-1, max(e_mem, e_slot)+1), carried (no advance) only for a Continue of the newest non-demoted QUIT generation"
    write_access: save-load-only (written by the Save/Load worker)

    why: "The join takes no timeout; a hung write would hang the frame at DEAD or at quit (CR-1a, exactly one thread boundary); a freed live Thread orphans its worker."

gdd_sync.new: typed Array[T] and Dictionary[K, V] values round-trip through var_to_bytes / bytes_to_var (probed; type preservation is not asserted); snapshots may use typed or untyped containers and the walk checks decoded element types

gdd_sync.old: or the owner's own canonical byte form where it publishes one (the Graph's `canonical_bytes()`, LS-21), as raw bytes inside the container

gdd_sync.new: 64-bit hex is ADR-0005 Hex64.encode / Hex64.decode (exact 16 lowercase [0-9a-f] checked by a loop, then hex_decode + decode_s64); campaign_id is an opaque 32-char lowercase hex String never converted to an int; String.hex_to_int is banned (saturates, probed)

gdd_sync.old: `campaign.lock`, created with an exclusive open and holding the process id
gdd_sync.new: FileAccess.open(WRITE) is not exclusive (probed); the lock is a FileAccess handle held as a SaveService member for the campaign lifetime, tested by a rename probe run only when the file exists (missing = not held); pid is diagnostic; the probe/startup race is an accepted exposure; Windows-only best effort, deferrable to Alpha; Linux/Deck unverified

gdd_sync.new: add SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER after step 12 (tick_rate) and before step 13: header catalogue_version above the build's is INCOMPATIBLE, no quarantine; catalogue_hash never gates

decisions.chosen: State reference-sharing as fact (probed); enforce immutability by ownership transfer: no retained alias or .duplicate()/.duplicate(true), worker never mutates an argument, optional shallow make_read_only, alias unit test
decisions.reason: Engine does not protect packed arrays; ADR-0005 already says they alias by reference; the old copy-on-write rationale was false

decisions.chosen: Option (a): two alternating 12-byte files (epoch, seq, CRC32) overwritten in place when older; no rename, no remove; campaign.json keeps rename-over as a recorded accepted exposure
decisions.reason: Rename-over is probably remove-then-rename on Windows; a missing epoch file would rebuild to a lower value and replay threat draws, which reopens the reroll hole on the one value where loss is exploitable

decisions.point: SaveHost placement and observation point (T1, TD-10, TD-09)
decisions.chosen: Thin Node in src/game/save_host.gd at ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE (-40) calling a tree-free RefCounted SaveService.poll_frame(); frame poll after the driver is the only observation point; polling of monotonic counters, no subscription
decisions.reason: ADR-0010 bans Node/_process in src/save/; no control-plane end-of-tick callback exists; a snapshot request is served before any tick so end-of-frame reads equal captured state

decisions.chosen: SaveHost sets auto_accept_quit false and routes WM_CLOSE_REQUEST / WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST by kernel state to a non-blocking polled flow; request_shutdown is the only place get_tree().quit() is reached
decisions.reason: Default auto-accept would cut a write in flight (probed 0.68 s exit); ADR-0001 owns the transition, ADR-0030 the UI

decisions.point: Control-plane shape and expected hash (E4, T2, TD-05)
decisions.chosen: request_snapshot() -> void with result via the outcome handler returning CompletionToken; snapshot outcome carries kernel-computed uncached T, world_seed, state_hash and per-block block_state_hash/enc_len; request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash: int, has_expected_hash: bool); Save/Load hashes only payload_sha256, trailer and registry_epoch
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0002; Variant/null breaks typed interfaces and 0 is a legal H64

decisions.point: Hex codec and canonical bytes (T6, TD-25, E5)
decisions.chosen: Use ADR-0005 Hex64 (exact-width lowercase loop before hex_decode, resize(8) before encode_s64); campaign_id is an opaque lowercase 32-char String with a local loop check; canonical-bytes embedding, OQ-I and the LS-21 sync dropped
decisions.reason: One owner for 64-bit encoding and canonical encoding; hex_decode accepts uppercase and logs on bad input (probed)

decisions.chosen: SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT (Windows template_release; Linux only for g; f synthetic 14-block fixture incl. walk timing) gates Accept; SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE on real owner blocks gates the Vertical Slice
decisions.reason: Owner blocks cannot exist before Accept because stories on a Proposed ADR are blocked; Linux is needed only for g and the Deck half of f

decisions.chosen: Capture is always uncached; PROFILE trigger compares uncached block_state_hash from the outcome; rung 1 is deferred, off by default, touch-serial based, needing a TD ruling and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment; no dirty-key dependency
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 5.4 and ADR-0004 section 7 forbid cached hashes and dirty keys on a decision path

decisions.chosen: Every millisecond timeout reads the injected Clock port (FakeClock in tests); created_unix and displayed time come from the WallClock port (src/save/wall_clock.gd, impl src/game/system_wall_clock.gd) and are display metadata only
decisions.reason: SIM-02 bans wall time in src/ outside the allow-list; generation number is the only order

decisions.chosen: Target at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes in SAVE-WRK-1 f, walk on the hot-copy worker when possible, MAX_DECODE_NODES provisionally 100 000
decisions.reason: GDScript walk at 250 000 nodes could cost 100 ms or more at the death stub; unmeasured so the bound is lowered until measured

decisions.chosen: PROFILE file mechanism specified but built at the first PROFILE block (Alpha); campaign.lock best effort and deferrable; settings persistence out of scope (ADR-0030, via an injected port implemented in src/save/); appendix move declined
decisions.reason: Zero PROFILE blocks ship at MVP; display settings are host-local Chart Table state; moving tables would break section cross-references

decisions.point: Pause during the death-stub epoch wait (T11)
decisions.chosen: Latch refuses only Save/Load's own capture requests and further restore triggers; pause suppression while DEAD (ADR-0030) or request_restore legal from PAUSED (ADR-0003) is recorded as OQ-J with a test
decisions.reason: Save/Load cannot refuse pause requests issued from PauseGate's own ControlHandle

decisions.chosen: Re-traced against tr-registry.yaml and the matrix: 65 baseline + 21 decided here + 4 Partial (033, 038, 039, 040) + 10 owned elsewhere = 100 rows; decisions added for header seats (037) and READ_ONLY (028)
decisions.reason: The matrix and registry plan more TRs for ADR-0006 than tr-baseline.md lists

open_questions: OQ-A: kernel owner must confirm the OQ-14 ruling (atomic SAVING, one over-budget frame per autosave); rung 1 stays deferred and off by default pending a TD ruling on SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (ADR-0005 OQ-10) and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment
OQ-D: campaign.lock is Windows-only best effort and deferrable to Alpha; decide at Alpha whether it ships and whether Linux/Deck needs a second mechanism
OQ-E: whether moving storage to canonical TLV (format_version 2) is worth it once ADR-0005 is Accepted; revisit at VS-A size review
OQ-G: ADR-0010 section 8.6 must allow-list the ~Thread exit WARNING / ObjectDB leak report and the bytes_to_var engine ERROR lines in the re-hashed fuzz configuration
OQ-H: co-op guest request_save carrier and guest-side restore_epoch view (ADR-0032)
OQ-J: pause during the death-stub epoch wait: PauseGate/Chart Table must suppress pause while a seat is DEAD (ADR-0030), or ADR-0003 must list request_restore from PAUSED
OQ-K: the Web Map ADR must supply web.state pod_arrived_seq and berthed_seq; until then those autosave triggers never fire
OQ-L: final MAX_DECODE_NODES and type-walk placement to be set from the SAVE-WRK-1 f timing (target at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes)

Engine claims still UNVERIFIED: Thread.start error codes, get_string_from_utf8 on invalid UTF-8, Thread freed while alive, worker blocked in a syscall or mid-store_buffer at exit, kill between remove and rename, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS poll in PAUSED/LOADING
Confirming engine and TD-ADR re-review is owed before Accept; ADR-0001, 0002, 0003, 0005, 0007 and 0010 must be Accepted and SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT passed

applied: T10 (partly: PROFILE file deferred to first PROFILE block, campaign.lock best effort and deferrable, settings out of scope)
TD-05 (alignment: async outcome handler, extended snapshot outcome, typed has_expected_hash)
TD-07 (alignment: BOOTING-only registrar facet, restore_epoch read only inside RngFacet.draw_epoch, packed arrays in payload are duplicates)
TD-12 (alignment: byte writers allowed in src/save/)
TD-27 (alignment: ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 under Depends On, tables injected, no data import)
TD-33 (Registry Candidates section added; restore_epoch single owner)

declined.id: T10 (part): move the per-block owned-elsewhere table and Migration Plan detail to an appendix
declined.reason: The sections are cross-referenced by number from the GDD syncs, the traceability matrix and the Review Log, and the Implementation Guidelines already give /create-control-manifest its extractable must/never rules, so splitting the file now would break references for little reader gain. The other T10 parts (PROFILE deferral, lock best-effort, settings out of scope) were applied.

    interface: "u32 in the per-slot pair user://saves/<campaign_id>/slot_epoch_a.bin and slot_epoch_b.bin (12 bytes each: u32 LE epoch, u32 LE seq, u32 LE hand-rolled CRC32 poly 0xEDB88320 of the first 8 bytes); the reader takes the valid file with the higher seq, the writer overwrites the older file in place (no rename, no remove); durable (EPOCH_DURABLE re-read) before request_restore; reaches the sim only as the request_restore / request_new_game argument and the read-only non-persisted non-hashed kernel.clock view (T, world_seed, restore_epoch), read only inside RngFacet.draw_epoch; each WORLD generation header carries a read-only write-time recovery copy; advance = min(2^32-1, max(e_mem, e_slot)+1), carried (no advance) only for a Continue of the newest non-demoted QUIT generation; single registry entry, ADR-0005 references it"
    write_access: save-load-only (written by the Save/Load worker)
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: save_worker_thread
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: save_worker_thread
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed; SAVE-WRK-1 confirms
    api: "one Thread per WriteJob (RefCounted holding the Thread and a Mutex-guarded status record), started with thread.start(WriteWorker.run.bind(...)) whose Error is checked; ownership transfer of handed-over objects (no retained alias, or .duplicate() / .duplicate(true); the worker never mutates, appends to or resizes an argument); only pre-globalised absolute paths; jobs kept in SaveService.jobs until reaped; main thread polls is_alive() and calls wait_to_finish() only on a dead thread; Save & Quit polls under SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS on the injected Clock then request_shutdown; abandoned jobs are never killed"
    not: "WorkerThreadPool; joining a live thread; call_deferred / set_deferred / call_thread_safe; Callable(WriteWorker, \"run\"); passing the worker a Node, block, read view or live-state container; dropping a live job"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    reason: "Packed arrays, Arrays and Dictionaries are reference-shared in GDScript (probed 2026-10-28), so immutability is by ownership transfer; Thread.wait_to_finish takes no timeout; a stuck disk must cost a stale file, not a stuck frame; a live sleeping thread did not delay exit past 0.68 s"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: object_or_resource_in_save_payload
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: object_or_resource_in_save_payload
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "No save, snapshot, profile or staged payload contains an Object, Resource, StringName, Vector2i or other vector/rect, Callable, Signal, RID, NodePath or non-finite float; the type walk enforces it at write (VERIFYING) and at load; var_to_bytes_with_objects, bytes_to_var_with_objects and Resource-based saves are never used."
    why: "var_to_bytes silently encodes an Object as EncodedObjectAsID (probed 2026-10-28), so the encoder is not a defence; a .tres can embed scripts."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: join_live_save_thread_or_workerthreadpool
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: join_live_save_thread_or_workerthreadpool
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "Nothing calls wait_to_finish on a Thread that is still alive, uses WorkerThreadPool for the save writer, drops a live WriteJob, or blocks the main thread on save I/O; Thread is legal only inside src/save/, one per WriteJob."
    why: "The join takes no timeout; a hung write would hang the frame at DEAD or at quit (CR-1a, exactly one thread boundary); a freed live Thread orphans its worker."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

    why: "Packed arrays, Arrays and Dictionaries are reference-shared across threads in GDScript (probed 2026-10-28); there is no copy-on-write protection."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: hex_to_int_on_64bit_field

registry_candidates.name: restore_epoch_in_hash_or_snapshot
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: restore_epoch_in_hash_or_snapshot
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "restore_epoch is never inside a block snapshot payload, a state_hash or block hash input, or a rewritten generation file; request_restore is called only after EPOCH_DURABLE (or the logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE failure path); a step-back, demotion, quarantine or lost manifest never lowers it."

gdd_sync.old: encoded with `var_to_bytes(dict)` (the form that does not encode objects)
gdd_sync.new: var_to_bytes DOES encode an Object, as an EncodedObjectAsID (probed 2026-10-28); the defence is the bounded type walk rejecting TYPE_OBJECT plus the write-side VERIFYING decode and walk, not the encoder

gdd_sync.old: `snapshot()` uses untyped containers until the spike resolves typed-container encoding [UNV]
gdd_sync.new: typed Array[T] and Dictionary[K, V] values round-trip through var_to_bytes / bytes_to_var (probed; type preservation is not asserted); snapshots may use typed or untyped containers and the walk checks decoded element types

gdd_sync.old: or the owner's own canonical byte form where it publishes one (the Graph's `canonical_bytes()`, LS-21), as raw bytes inside the container
gdd_sync.new: delete the clause: there is one payload form, a Dictionary; canonical bytes are produced by the kernel (ADR-0005 section 3.1) and never stored; the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays

gdd_sync.old: numeric values below 2^53 (S-1) for every block payload
gdd_sync.new: payload ints may be native int64 (var_to_bytes is exact, probed with 2^53+1); the strict-below-2^53 rule and the string convention apply to the JSON header and dump-save; a field that may reach 2^53 is declared int64 in the owner schema; two 32-bit halves remain legal

gdd_sync.old: hex decoding is exact-width ... no general string-to-int parse
gdd_sync.new: 64-bit hex is ADR-0005 Hex64.encode / Hex64.decode (exact 16 lowercase [0-9a-f] checked by a loop, then hex_decode + decode_s64); campaign_id is an opaque 32-char lowercase hex String never converted to an int; String.hex_to_int is banned (saturates, probed)

gdd_sync.old: `campaign.lock`, created with an exclusive open and holding the process id
gdd_sync.new: FileAccess.open(WRITE) is not exclusive (probed); the lock is a FileAccess handle held as a SaveService member for the campaign lifetime, tested by a rename probe run only when the file exists (missing = not held); pid is diagnostic; the probe/startup race is an accepted exposure; Windows-only best effort, deferrable to Alpha; Linux/Deck unverified

gdd_sync.old: T-5 steps 1 to 23 (no catalogue check)
gdd_sync.new: add SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER after step 12 (tick_rate) and before step 13: header catalogue_version above the build's is INCOMPATIBLE, no quarantine; catalogue_hash never gates

gdd_sync.old: the physical reason encoding stays OQ-27
gdd_sync.new: quarantine reason is in the file name quarantine/g<generation>_<REASON>_<k>.sav; retire_campaign moves the directory to user://saves_retired/<campaign_id>/; OQ-27 closed

gdd_sync.old: OQ-14 / SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS open
gdd_sync.new: annotate: atomic SAVING kept, one over-budget frame per autosave accepted pending SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT f (synthetic) and SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (real blocks); rungs: (1) deferred and off by default, kernel skips snapshot() for a block whose ADR-0005 cache entry is valid by touch serial, needs a TD ruling and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment, no dirty-key dependency; (2) encode on the worker; (3) split capture only with a kernel amendment

gdd_sync.old: `Thread.wait_to_finish` ... a join at the DEAD boundary; Save & Quit wait
gdd_sync.new: record the probed result: a live thread does not delay process exit (0.68 s with an 8 s sleeping worker; ~Thread WARNING and ObjectDB leak report); Save & Quit is bounded polling under SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS, never a join; the window close button, Alt+F4 and OS shutdown take the same path (auto_accept_quit false, SaveHost, request_shutdown is the only quit)

gdd_sync.old: never uses `var_to_bytes` or a Resource for saves
gdd_sync.new: never uses Resource for saves and never uses var_to_bytes bytes as hash input; the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays, storage is var_to_bytes, hash input is ADR-0005's TLV of the same payload (ADR-0005 Migration item 2; no canonical_bytes embedding)

gdd_sync.old: excluded from the snapshot header and all hashes
gdd_sync.new: excluded from the kernel snapshot payload and every hash; the container header carries a read-only write-time recovery copy covered only by the file trailer

gdd_sync.file: design/gdd/player-controller-input.md PC-17; ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md LY-26 a; tr-baseline TR-cmd-016, TR-pc-020, TR-section-007
gdd_sync.old: restore() is a whole-block replace / swaps whole tables from scratch
gdd_sync.new: restore validates into scratch, then replaces the block's contents in place (copy into the existing block object, never replace the object); root rule ADR-0003 section 2

gdd_sync.file: design/gdd/suit-and-equipment.md SE-34 / AC-SE-35 and tr-baseline TR-suit-009
gdd_sync.old: plain-data `snapshot()` (no Vector2i, StringName keys, typed containers)
gdd_sync.new: String or int keys only; StringName keys and values are banned from files by the type walk; typed containers are allowed (their values round-trip)

gdd_sync.file: owner GDDs describing restore() returning (ok, reason, detail) (ADR-0003 sync; TR-saveload-033)
gdd_sync.old: two-phase `restore` returning `(ok, reason, detail)`
gdd_sync.new: failure is reported through ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*) with the owner's domain code; Save/Load maps the kernel load_failed trigger to the RESTORE_FAILED class

gdd_sync.old: 64-bit values as two 32-bit halves or strings, never as JSON numbers
gdd_sync.new: halves or strings remain legal; native int64 is also accepted in the binary payload (exact); the convention is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON (header, dump-save)

gdd_sync.old: JSON-parsed integer-valued floats are accepted and re-cast to int

gdd_sync.old: `slot_epoch.bin` (8 bytes: u32 epoch + u32 CRC32), temp, flush, rename over the live name; a leftover `slot_epoch.tmp` is deleted
gdd_sync.new: the pair slot_epoch_a.bin / slot_epoch_b.bin (12 bytes: u32 epoch, u32 seq, u32 CRC32 of the first 8), reader takes the valid file with the higher seq, writer overwrites the older file in place with flush, close and CRC re-read; no rename, no remove, no .tmp; rebuild from the generation header copy only when both files are invalid

gdd_sync.old: per-block hash field (unnamed or cached-hash wording); MAX_DECODE_NODES 250 000; created_unix
gdd_sync.new: the per-block hash field is named block_state_hash beside enc_len and is the kernel's uncached capture value; header seats list (non-empty, unique, in range, covers every PER_PLAYER key; no peer id; TR-saveload-037); MAX_DECODE_NODES provisional 100 000 until SAVE-WRK-1 f measures the walk (250 000 kept as the ceiling); created_unix is display metadata from the WallClock port, never an ordering, gate or hash input

gdd_sync.old: provisional end-of-tick callback channel for the observation set
gdd_sync.new: Save/Load polls monotonic counters and read views once per frame in poll_frame (SaveHost at HOST_SERVICE), no subscription and no end-of-tick callback; add conditional web.state members pod_arrived_seq and berthed_seq (required of the Web Map ADR); an event whose owner read is absent never fires; last-seen copies are re-read after a load

gdd_sync.old: a `restore_pending` latch refuses every capture and pause request
gdd_sync.new: the restore_pending latch refuses Save/Load's own capture requests and further restore triggers (SL_LOAD_REENTRANT); pause suppression while a seat is DEAD belongs to PauseGate or the Chart Table (ADR-0030), or request_restore is legal from PAUSED (ADR-0003); a test pauses during the epoch wait

gdd_sync.old: PROFILE file mechanism and campaign.lock built at MVP
gdd_sync.new: the PROFILE file mechanism (ring of one, .bak, change-detection trigger on uncached block_state_hash) is deferred to the first PROFILE block (not before Alpha) with file_kind and persist_scope reserved; campaign.lock is Windows-only best effort and deferrable to Alpha; settings persistence is out of scope (host-local, ADR-0030)

decisions.chosen: State reference-sharing as fact (probed); enforce immutability by ownership transfer: no retained alias or .duplicate()/.duplicate(true), worker never mutates an argument, optional shallow make_read_only, alias unit test
decisions.reason: Engine does not protect packed arrays; ADR-0005 already says they alias by reference; the old copy-on-write rationale was false

decisions.chosen: Option (a): two alternating 12-byte files (epoch, seq, CRC32) overwritten in place when older; no rename, no remove; campaign.json keeps rename-over as a recorded accepted exposure
decisions.reason: Rename-over is probably remove-then-rename on Windows; a missing epoch file would rebuild to a lower value and replay threat draws, which reopens the reroll hole on the one value where loss is exploitable

decisions.point: SaveHost placement and observation point (T1, TD-10, TD-09)
decisions.chosen: Thin Node in src/game/save_host.gd at ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE (-40) calling a tree-free RefCounted SaveService.poll_frame(); frame poll after the driver is the only observation point; polling of monotonic counters, no subscription
decisions.reason: ADR-0010 bans Node/_process in src/save/; no control-plane end-of-tick callback exists; a snapshot request is served before any tick so end-of-frame reads equal captured state

decisions.chosen: SaveHost sets auto_accept_quit false and routes WM_CLOSE_REQUEST / WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST by kernel state to a non-blocking polled flow; request_shutdown is the only place get_tree().quit() is reached
decisions.reason: Default auto-accept would cut a write in flight (probed 0.68 s exit); ADR-0001 owns the transition, ADR-0030 the UI

decisions.point: Control-plane shape and expected hash (E4, T2, TD-05)
decisions.chosen: request_snapshot() -> void with result via the outcome handler returning CompletionToken; snapshot outcome carries kernel-computed uncached T, world_seed, state_hash and per-block block_state_hash/enc_len; request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash: int, has_expected_hash: bool); Save/Load hashes only payload_sha256, trailer and registry_epoch
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0002; Variant/null breaks typed interfaces and 0 is a legal H64

decisions.point: Hex codec and canonical bytes (T6, TD-25, E5)
decisions.chosen: Use ADR-0005 Hex64 (exact-width lowercase loop before hex_decode, resize(8) before encode_s64); campaign_id is an opaque lowercase 32-char String with a local loop check; canonical-bytes embedding, OQ-I and the LS-21 sync dropped
decisions.reason: One owner for 64-bit encoding and canonical encoding; hex_decode accepts uppercase and logs on bad input (probed)

decisions.chosen: SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT (Windows template_release; Linux only for g; f synthetic 14-block fixture incl. walk timing) gates Accept; SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE on real owner blocks gates the Vertical Slice
decisions.reason: Owner blocks cannot exist before Accept because stories on a Proposed ADR are blocked; Linux is needed only for g and the Deck half of f

decisions.chosen: Capture is always uncached; PROFILE trigger compares uncached block_state_hash from the outcome; rung 1 is deferred, off by default, touch-serial based, needing a TD ruling and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment; no dirty-key dependency
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 5.4 and ADR-0004 section 7 forbid cached hashes and dirty keys on a decision path

decisions.chosen: Every millisecond timeout reads the injected Clock port (FakeClock in tests); created_unix and displayed time come from the WallClock port (src/save/wall_clock.gd, impl src/game/system_wall_clock.gd) and are display metadata only
decisions.reason: SIM-02 bans wall time in src/ outside the allow-list; generation number is the only order

decisions.chosen: Target at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes in SAVE-WRK-1 f, walk on the hot-copy worker when possible, MAX_DECODE_NODES provisionally 100 000
decisions.reason: GDScript walk at 250 000 nodes could cost 100 ms or more at the death stub; unmeasured so the bound is lowered until measured

decisions.chosen: PROFILE file mechanism specified but built at the first PROFILE block (Alpha); campaign.lock best effort and deferrable; settings persistence out of scope (ADR-0030, via an injected port implemented in src/save/); appendix move declined
decisions.reason: Zero PROFILE blocks ship at MVP; display settings are host-local Chart Table state; moving tables would break section cross-references

decisions.point: Pause during the death-stub epoch wait (T11)
decisions.chosen: Latch refuses only Save/Load's own capture requests and further restore triggers; pause suppression while DEAD (ADR-0030) or request_restore legal from PAUSED (ADR-0003) is recorded as OQ-J with a test
decisions.reason: Save/Load cannot refuse pause requests issued from PauseGate's own ControlHandle

decisions.chosen: Re-traced against tr-registry.yaml and the matrix: 65 baseline + 21 decided here + 4 Partial (033, 038, 039, 040) + 10 owned elsewhere = 100 rows; decisions added for header seats (037) and READ_ONLY (028)
decisions.reason: The matrix and registry plan more TRs for ADR-0006 than tr-baseline.md lists

open_questions: OQ-A: kernel owner must confirm the OQ-14 ruling (atomic SAVING, one over-budget frame per autosave); rung 1 stays deferred and off by default pending a TD ruling on SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (ADR-0005 OQ-10) and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment
OQ-D: campaign.lock is Windows-only best effort and deferrable to Alpha; decide at Alpha whether it ships and whether Linux/Deck needs a second mechanism
OQ-E: whether moving storage to canonical TLV (format_version 2) is worth it once ADR-0005 is Accepted; revisit at VS-A size review
OQ-G: ADR-0010 section 8.6 must allow-list the ~Thread exit WARNING / ObjectDB leak report and the bytes_to_var engine ERROR lines in the re-hashed fuzz configuration
OQ-H: co-op guest request_save carrier and guest-side restore_epoch view (ADR-0032)
OQ-J: pause during the death-stub epoch wait: PauseGate/Chart Table must suppress pause while a seat is DEAD (ADR-0030), or ADR-0003 must list request_restore from PAUSED
OQ-K: the Web Map ADR must supply web.state pod_arrived_seq and berthed_seq; until then those autosave triggers never fire
OQ-L: final MAX_DECODE_NODES and type-walk placement to be set from the SAVE-WRK-1 f timing (target at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes)

Engine claims still UNVERIFIED: Thread.start error codes, get_string_from_utf8 on invalid UTF-8, Thread freed while alive, worker blocked in a syscall or mid-store_buffer at exit, kill between remove and rename, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS poll in PAUSED/LOADING
Confirming engine and TD-ADR re-review is owed before Accept; ADR-0001, 0002, 0003, 0005, 0007 and 0010 must be Accepted and SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT passed

applied: T10 (partly: PROFILE file deferred to first PROFILE block, campaign.lock best effort and deferrable, settings out of scope)
TD-05 (alignment: async outcome handler, extended snapshot outcome, typed has_expected_hash)
TD-07 (alignment: BOOTING-only registrar facet, restore_epoch read only inside RngFacet.draw_epoch, packed arrays in payload are duplicates)
TD-12 (alignment: byte writers allowed in src/save/)
TD-27 (alignment: ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 under Depends On, tables injected, no data import)

declined.reason: The sections are cross-referenced by number from the GDD syncs, the traceability matrix and the Review Log, and the Implementation Guidelines already give /create-control-manifest its extractable must/never rules, so splitting the file now would break references for little reader gain. The other T10 parts (PROFILE deferral, lock best-effort, settings out of scope) were applied.

    api: "var_to_bytes(dictionary) per block, decoded with bytes_to_var only after trailer, block table and payload_sha256 pass, then a bounded type walk (MAX_DECODE_DEPTH 16, MAX_DECODE_NODES provisional 100000) that rejects TYPE_OBJECT, StringName, vectors and non-finite floats; the worker re-decodes and walks what it wrote in VERIFYING"
    not: "var_to_bytes_with_objects / bytes_to_var_with_objects; Resource, .tres, .res, ResourceLoader or load() for a save; JSON or base64 payloads; trusting the encoder to refuse objects (it encodes an Object as EncodedObjectAsID, probed 2026-10-28); storing canonical bytes"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    reason: "Native, exact int64 (probed 2^53+1), one decode path and one fuzz target; stored bytes are not canonical, so state equality is state_hash and hash input is ADR-0005's canonical encoding"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: hex64_header_decode
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: hex64_header_decode
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    api: "ADR-0005 Hex64.encode / Hex64.decode (src/shared/det/): exactly 16 lowercase [0-9a-f] validated by a loop, then hex_decode + decode_s64; resize(8) before encode_s64; campaign_id is an opaque 32-char lowercase hex String validated by a loop and never converted to an int; header integers must be integral and strictly < 2^53"
    not: "String.hex_to_int (saturates to INT64_MAX with an engine error, probed 2026-10-28); to_int(); hex_decode on unvalidated text (accepts uppercase, logs on bad input); any 64-bit or hashed value as a JSON number; a second 64-bit codec in src/save/"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    reason: "JSON.parse returns float for every number (2^53+1 parses to 2^53, probed); top-bit-set values read as negative GDScript ints by design"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: save_worker_thread
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: save_worker_thread
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed; SAVE-WRK-1 confirms
    api: "one Thread per WriteJob (RefCounted holding the Thread and a Mutex-guarded status record), started with thread.start(WriteWorker.run.bind(...)) whose Error is checked; ownership transfer of handed-over objects (no retained alias, or .duplicate() / .duplicate(true); the worker never mutates, appends to or resizes an argument); only pre-globalised absolute paths; jobs kept in SaveService.jobs until reaped; main thread polls is_alive() and calls wait_to_finish() only on a dead thread; Save & Quit polls under SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS on the injected Clock then request_shutdown; abandoned jobs are never killed"
    not: "WorkerThreadPool; joining a live thread; call_deferred / set_deferred / call_thread_safe; Callable(WriteWorker, \"run\"); passing the worker a Node, block, read view or live-state container; dropping a live job"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    reason: "Packed arrays, Arrays and Dictionaries are reference-shared in GDScript (probed 2026-10-28), so immutability is by ownership transfer; Thread.wait_to_finish takes no timeout; a stuck disk must cost a stale file, not a stuck frame; a live sleeping thread did not delay exit past 0.68 s"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: save_file_swap
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: save_file_swap
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    api: "generation swap: write gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp, flush, close, re-open, re-hash, decode + walk; rename the position's old file to .bak; rename .tmp to the now-absent gen_k.sav; re-hash; delete .bak; every store_* and rename result checked; campaign.json uses temp + rename-over as an accepted non-atomic exposure; slot_epoch uses two alternating files overwritten in place (no rename, no remove)"
    not: "rename-over-existing for generations or the epoch (probably remove-then-rename on Windows, so not atomic, UNVERIFIED); describing rename-over as atomic or 'old file intact' across a crash; overwriting a generation in place; deleting a generation before its successor verified"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    reason: "Every partial state is recoverable by T-6; sharing violations leave the target intact; a valid epoch file always exists"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: campaign_lock
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: campaign_lock
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed; Linux/Deck behaviour UNVERIFIED (SAVE-WRK-1 g)
    api: "hold a FileAccess handle on campaign.lock as a SaveService member for the campaign lifetime (never a local, never reassigned; is_open() asserted per frame poll); a second process renames the file to campaign.lock.probe and back (only when the file exists; missing means not held); failure means held, so open READ_ONLY; Windows-only best effort, deferrable to Alpha"
    not: "an exclusive FileAccess.open (WRITE-open is not exclusive, probed 2026-10-28); OS.is_process_running liveness checks on a foreign pid"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    reason: "Held files cannot be renamed or removed on Windows (probed); the handle dies with the process so no stale lock exists; the probe/startup race is an accepted exposure"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: save_close_request
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- purpose: save_close_request
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed; SAVE-WRK-1 e confirms
    api: "SaveHost sets get_tree().auto_accept_quit = false and forwards NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST / NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST to SaveService.on_close_request(), routed by kernel state (TR-saveload-039), polled under SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS, never blocking; request_shutdown is the only place get_tree().quit() is reached"
    not: "the default auto-accepted quit; get_tree().quit() from Save/Load or the host; a blocking wait for the writer"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    reason: "The window X, Alt+F4 and OS shutdown otherwise exit at once and cut a write in flight (probed exit 0.68 s)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: ""

registry_candidates.name: object_or_resource_in_save_payload
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: object_or_resource_in_save_payload
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "No save, snapshot, profile or staged payload contains an Object, Resource, StringName, Vector2i or other vector/rect, Callable, Signal, RID, NodePath or non-finite float; the type walk enforces it at write (VERIFYING) and at load; var_to_bytes_with_objects, bytes_to_var_with_objects and Resource-based saves are never used."
    why: "var_to_bytes silently encodes an Object as EncodedObjectAsID (probed 2026-10-28), so the encoder is not a defence; a .tres can embed scripts."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: join_live_save_thread_or_workerthreadpool
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: join_live_save_thread_or_workerthreadpool
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "Nothing calls wait_to_finish on a Thread that is still alive, uses WorkerThreadPool for the save writer, drops a live WriteJob, or blocks the main thread on save I/O; Thread is legal only inside src/save/, one per WriteJob."
    why: "The join takes no timeout; a hung write would hang the frame at DEAD or at quit (CR-1a, exactly one thread boundary); a freed live Thread orphans its worker."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: alias_after_save_handoff
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: alias_after_save_handoff
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "After a buffer is handed to the save worker the main thread keeps no alias to it, or hands over .duplicate() / .duplicate(true); neither side appends to, resizes or mutates a handed-over object."
    why: "Packed arrays, Arrays and Dictionaries are reference-shared across threads in GDScript (probed 2026-10-28); there is no copy-on-write protection."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: hex_to_int_on_64bit_field
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: hex_to_int_on_64bit_field
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "No 64-bit header or hash field is parsed with String.hex_to_int, int() or to_int(), or read from a JSON number; decode with ADR-0005 Hex64.decode after its exact-width lowercase pre-check."
    why: "hex_to_int saturates at INT64_MAX with an engine error, hex_decode accepts uppercase, and JSON numbers are floats that corrupt values from 2^53 up (probed 2026-10-28)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: restore_epoch_in_hash_or_snapshot
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: restore_epoch_in_hash_or_snapshot
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "restore_epoch is never inside a block snapshot payload, a state_hash or block hash input, or a rewritten generation file; request_restore is called only after EPOCH_DURABLE (or the logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE failure path); a step-back, demotion, quarantine or lost manifest never lowers it."
    why: "Keeps every generation immutable after VERIFYING so REBASED baselines hold, and keeps quit and death from being a reroll oracle (R13/R14)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28

registry_candidates.name: wall_clock_in_save_ordering
registry_candidates.entry_yaml:
- pattern: wall_clock_in_save_ordering
    status: active           # ADR-0006 is Proposed
    description: "created_unix and the SaveInfo time (WallClock port) are display metadata only; no ordering, gate, hash or sim input reads them; every millisecond timeout reads the injected Clock port."
    why: "The generation number is the only order; wall time is banned in src/ outside the SIM-02 allow-list (ADR-0010, TD-11)."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0006-save-container-generations-versioning-and-restore-epoch.md
    added: 2026-10-28
