gdd_sync.old: encoded with `var_to_bytes(dict)` (the form that does not encode objects)
gdd_sync.new: var_to_bytes DOES encode an Object, as an EncodedObjectAsID (probed 2026-10-28); the defence is the bounded type walk rejecting TYPE_OBJECT plus the write-side VERIFYING decode and walk, not the encoder

gdd_sync.old: `snapshot()` uses untyped containers until the spike resolves typed-container encoding [UNV]
gdd_sync.new: typed Array[T] and Dictionary[K, V] values round-trip through var_to_bytes / bytes_to_var (probed; type preservation is not asserted); snapshots may use typed or untyped containers and the walk checks decoded element types

gdd_sync.old: or the owner's own canonical byte form where it publishes one (the Graph's `canonical_bytes()`, LS-21), as raw bytes inside the container
gdd_sync.new: delete the clause: there is one payload form, a Dictionary; canonical bytes are produced by the kernel (ADR-0005 section 3.1) and never stored; the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays

gdd_sync.old: numeric values below 2^53 (S-1) for every block payload
gdd_sync.new: payload ints may be native int64 (var_to_bytes is exact, probed with 2^53+1); the strict-below-2^53 rule and the string convention apply to the JSON header and dump-save; a field that may reach 2^53 is declared int64 in the owner schema; two 32-bit halves remain legal

gdd_sync.old: hex decoding is exact-width ... no general string-to-int parse
gdd_sync.new: 64-bit hex is ADR-0005 Hex64.encode / Hex64.decode (exact 16 lowercase [0-9a-f] checked by a loop, then hex_decode + decode_s64); campaign_id is an opaque 32-char lowercase hex String never converted to an int; String.hex_to_int is banned (saturates, probed)

gdd_sync.old: `campaign.lock`, created with an exclusive open and holding the process id
gdd_sync.new: FileAccess.open(WRITE) is not exclusive (probed); the lock is a FileAccess handle held as a SaveService member for the campaign lifetime, tested by a rename probe run only when the file exists (missing = not held); pid is diagnostic; the probe/startup race is an accepted exposure; Windows-only best effort, deferrable to Alpha; Linux/Deck unverified

gdd_sync.old: T-5 steps 1 to 23 (no catalogue check)
gdd_sync.new: add SL_PRECHECK_CATALOGUE_NEWER after step 12 (tick_rate) and before step 13: header catalogue_version above the build's is INCOMPATIBLE, no quarantine; catalogue_hash never gates

gdd_sync.old: the physical reason encoding stays OQ-27
gdd_sync.new: quarantine reason is in the file name quarantine/g<generation>_<REASON>_<k>.sav; retire_campaign moves the directory to user://saves_retired/<campaign_id>/; OQ-27 closed

gdd_sync.old: OQ-14 / SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS open
gdd_sync.new: annotate: atomic SAVING kept, one over-budget frame per autosave accepted pending SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT f (synthetic) and SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (real blocks); rungs: (1) deferred and off by default, kernel skips snapshot() for a block whose ADR-0005 cache entry is valid by touch serial, needs a TD ruling and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment, no dirty-key dependency; (2) encode on the worker; (3) split capture only with a kernel amendment

gdd_sync.old: `Thread.wait_to_finish` ... a join at the DEAD boundary; Save & Quit wait
gdd_sync.new: record the probed result: a live thread does not delay process exit (0.68 s with an 8 s sleeping worker; ~Thread WARNING and ObjectDB leak report); Save & Quit is bounded polling under SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS, never a join; the window close button, Alt+F4 and OS shutdown take the same path (auto_accept_quit false, SaveHost, request_shutdown is the only quit)

gdd_sync.old: never uses `var_to_bytes` or a Resource for saves
gdd_sync.new: never uses Resource for saves and never uses var_to_bytes bytes as hash input; the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays, storage is var_to_bytes, hash input is ADR-0005's TLV of the same payload (ADR-0005 Migration item 2; no canonical_bytes embedding)

gdd_sync.old: excluded from the snapshot header and all hashes
gdd_sync.new: excluded from the kernel snapshot payload and every hash; the container header carries a read-only write-time recovery copy covered only by the file trailer

gdd_sync.file: design/gdd/player-controller-input.md PC-17; ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md LY-26 a; tr-baseline TR-cmd-016, TR-pc-020, TR-section-007
gdd_sync.old: restore() is a whole-block replace / swaps whole tables from scratch
gdd_sync.new: restore validates into scratch, then replaces the block's contents in place (copy into the existing block object, never replace the object); root rule ADR-0003 section 2

gdd_sync.file: design/gdd/suit-and-equipment.md SE-34 / AC-SE-35 and tr-baseline TR-suit-009
gdd_sync.old: plain-data `snapshot()` (no Vector2i, StringName keys, typed containers)
gdd_sync.new: String or int keys only; StringName keys and values are banned from files by the type walk; typed containers are allowed (their values round-trip)

gdd_sync.file: owner GDDs describing restore() returning (ok, reason, detail) (ADR-0003 sync; TR-saveload-033)
gdd_sync.old: two-phase `restore` returning `(ok, reason, detail)`
gdd_sync.new: failure is reported through ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*) with the owner's domain code; Save/Load maps the kernel load_failed trigger to the RESTORE_FAILED class

gdd_sync.old: 64-bit values as two 32-bit halves or strings, never as JSON numbers
gdd_sync.new: halves or strings remain legal; native int64 is also accepted in the binary payload (exact); the convention is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON (header, dump-save)

gdd_sync.old: JSON-parsed integer-valued floats are accepted and re-cast to int
gdd_sync.new: binary payload ints are exact, so a float where an int is expected is a SHAPE failure; the re-cast clause applies only to dev JSON fixtures

gdd_sync.file: docs/architecture/architecture.md (Spikes that gate ADRs, Save worker row; Data Flow 6 and 7)
gdd_sync.old: Save worker (DirAccess.rename over an existing file on Windows ... snapshot hitch size)
gdd_sync.new: split into SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT (a, b, c, d, e, h, i on a Windows template_release; g on any Linux build; f with a synthetic 14-block fixture) and SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (f on real owner blocks, RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK; gates the Vertical Slice, not Accept); add the probe results; Save & Quit polls rather than joins and the window-close request takes the same path

gdd_sync.old: `slot_epoch.bin` (8 bytes: u32 epoch + u32 CRC32), temp, flush, rename over the live name; a leftover `slot_epoch.tmp` is deleted
gdd_sync.new: the pair slot_epoch_a.bin / slot_epoch_b.bin (12 bytes: u32 epoch, u32 seq, u32 CRC32 of the first 8), reader takes the valid file with the higher seq, writer overwrites the older file in place with flush, close and CRC re-read; no rename, no remove, no .tmp; rebuild from the generation header copy only when both files are invalid

gdd_sync.old: per-block hash field (unnamed or cached-hash wording); MAX_DECODE_NODES 250 000; created_unix
gdd_sync.new: the per-block hash field is named block_state_hash beside enc_len and is the kernel's uncached capture value; header seats list (non-empty, unique, in range, covers every PER_PLAYER key; no peer id; TR-saveload-037); MAX_DECODE_NODES provisional 100 000 until SAVE-WRK-1 f measures the walk (250 000 kept as the ceiling); created_unix is display metadata from the WallClock port, never an ordering, gate or hash input

gdd_sync.old: provisional end-of-tick callback channel for the observation set
gdd_sync.new: Save/Load polls monotonic counters and read views once per frame in poll_frame (SaveHost at HOST_SERVICE), no subscription and no end-of-tick callback; add conditional web.state members pod_arrived_seq and berthed_seq (required of the Web Map ADR); an event whose owner read is absent never fires; last-seen copies are re-read after a load

gdd_sync.old: a `restore_pending` latch refuses every capture and pause request
gdd_sync.new: the restore_pending latch refuses Save/Load's own capture requests and further restore triggers (SL_LOAD_REENTRANT); pause suppression while a seat is DEAD belongs to PauseGate or the Chart Table (ADR-0030), or request_restore is legal from PAUSED (ADR-0003); a test pauses during the epoch wait

gdd_sync.old: PROFILE file mechanism and campaign.lock built at MVP
gdd_sync.new: the PROFILE file mechanism (ring of one, .bak, change-detection trigger on uncached block_state_hash) is deferred to the first PROFILE block (not before Alpha) with file_kind and persist_scope reserved; campaign.lock is Windows-only best effort and deferrable to Alpha; settings persistence is out of scope (host-local, ADR-0030)

decisions.chosen: State reference-sharing as fact (probed); enforce immutability by ownership transfer: no retained alias or .duplicate()/.duplicate(true), worker never mutates an argument, optional shallow make_read_only, alias unit test
decisions.reason: Engine does not protect packed arrays; ADR-0005 already says they alias by reference; the old copy-on-write rationale was false

decisions.chosen: Option (a): two alternating 12-byte files (epoch, seq, CRC32) overwritten in place when older; no rename, no remove; campaign.json keeps rename-over as a recorded accepted exposure
decisions.reason: Rename-over is probably remove-then-rename on Windows; a missing epoch file would rebuild to a lower value and replay threat draws, which reopens the reroll hole on the one value where loss is exploitable

decisions.point: SaveHost placement and observation point (T1, TD-10, TD-09)
decisions.chosen: Thin Node in src/game/save_host.gd at ProcessPriority.HOST_SERVICE (-40) calling a tree-free RefCounted SaveService.poll_frame(); frame poll after the driver is the only observation point; polling of monotonic counters, no subscription
decisions.reason: ADR-0010 bans Node/_process in src/save/; no control-plane end-of-tick callback exists; a snapshot request is served before any tick so end-of-frame reads equal captured state

decisions.chosen: SaveHost sets auto_accept_quit false and routes WM_CLOSE_REQUEST / WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST by kernel state to a non-blocking polled flow; request_shutdown is the only place get_tree().quit() is reached
decisions.reason: Default auto-accept would cut a write in flight (probed 0.68 s exit); ADR-0001 owns the transition, ADR-0030 the UI

decisions.point: Control-plane shape and expected hash (E4, T2, TD-05)
decisions.chosen: request_snapshot() -> void with result via the outcome handler returning CompletionToken; snapshot outcome carries kernel-computed uncached T, world_seed, state_hash and per-block block_state_hash/enc_len; request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash: int, has_expected_hash: bool); Save/Load hashes only payload_sha256, trailer and registry_epoch
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0002; Variant/null breaks typed interfaces and 0 is a legal H64

decisions.point: Hex codec and canonical bytes (T6, TD-25, E5)
decisions.chosen: Use ADR-0005 Hex64 (exact-width lowercase loop before hex_decode, resize(8) before encode_s64); campaign_id is an opaque lowercase 32-char String with a local loop check; canonical-bytes embedding, OQ-I and the LS-21 sync dropped
decisions.reason: One owner for 64-bit encoding and canonical encoding; hex_decode accepts uppercase and logs on bad input (probed)

decisions.chosen: SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT (Windows template_release; Linux only for g; f synthetic 14-block fixture incl. walk timing) gates Accept; SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE on real owner blocks gates the Vertical Slice
decisions.reason: Owner blocks cannot exist before Accept because stories on a Proposed ADR are blocked; Linux is needed only for g and the Deck half of f

decisions.chosen: Capture is always uncached; PROFILE trigger compares uncached block_state_hash from the outcome; rung 1 is deferred, off by default, touch-serial based, needing a TD ruling and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment; no dirty-key dependency
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 5.4 and ADR-0004 section 7 forbid cached hashes and dirty keys on a decision path

decisions.chosen: Every millisecond timeout reads the injected Clock port (FakeClock in tests); created_unix and displayed time come from the WallClock port (src/save/wall_clock.gd, impl src/game/system_wall_clock.gd) and are display metadata only
decisions.reason: SIM-02 bans wall time in src/ outside the allow-list; generation number is the only order

decisions.chosen: Target at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes in SAVE-WRK-1 f, walk on the hot-copy worker when possible, MAX_DECODE_NODES provisionally 100 000
decisions.reason: GDScript walk at 250 000 nodes could cost 100 ms or more at the death stub; unmeasured so the bound is lowered until measured

decisions.chosen: PROFILE file mechanism specified but built at the first PROFILE block (Alpha); campaign.lock best effort and deferrable; settings persistence out of scope (ADR-0030, via an injected port implemented in src/save/); appendix move declined
decisions.reason: Zero PROFILE blocks ship at MVP; display settings are host-local Chart Table state; moving tables would break section cross-references

decisions.point: Pause during the death-stub epoch wait (T11)
decisions.chosen: Latch refuses only Save/Load's own capture requests and further restore triggers; pause suppression while DEAD (ADR-0030) or request_restore legal from PAUSED (ADR-0003) is recorded as OQ-J with a test
decisions.reason: Save/Load cannot refuse pause requests issued from PauseGate's own ControlHandle

decisions.chosen: Re-traced against tr-registry.yaml and the matrix: 65 baseline + 21 decided here + 4 Partial (033, 038, 039, 040) + 10 owned elsewhere = 100 rows; decisions added for header seats (037) and READ_ONLY (028)

open_questions: OQ-A: kernel owner must confirm the OQ-14 ruling (atomic SAVING, one over-budget frame per autosave); rung 1 stays deferred and off by default pending a TD ruling on SAVE-WRK-1-SLICE (ADR-0005 OQ-10) and an ADR-0005 5.4 amendment
OQ-D: campaign.lock is Windows-only best effort and deferrable to Alpha; decide at Alpha whether it ships and whether Linux/Deck needs a second mechanism
OQ-E: whether moving storage to canonical TLV (format_version 2) is worth it once ADR-0005 is Accepted; revisit at VS-A size review
OQ-G: ADR-0010 section 8.6 must allow-list the ~Thread exit WARNING / ObjectDB leak report and the bytes_to_var engine ERROR lines in the re-hashed fuzz configuration
OQ-H: co-op guest request_save carrier and guest-side restore_epoch view (ADR-0032)
OQ-J: pause during the death-stub epoch wait: PauseGate/Chart Table must suppress pause while a seat is DEAD (ADR-0030), or ADR-0003 must list request_restore from PAUSED
OQ-K: the Web Map ADR must supply web.state pod_arrived_seq and berthed_seq; until then those autosave triggers never fire
OQ-L: final MAX_DECODE_NODES and type-walk placement to be set from the SAVE-WRK-1 f timing (target at most 4 ms at 30 000 nodes)

Engine claims still UNVERIFIED: Thread.start error codes, get_string_from_utf8 on invalid UTF-8, Thread freed while alive, worker blocked in a syscall or mid-store_buffer at exit, kill between remove and rename, PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS poll in PAUSED/LOADING
Confirming engine and TD-ADR re-review is owed before Accept; ADR-0001, 0002, 0003, 0005, 0007 and 0010 must be Accepted and SAVE-WRK-1-ACCEPT passed
